title: CFPB credit-card market terms and a two-tier credit system
discussion_signal: The post interprets CFPB card-market findings as a split between prime borrowers receiving rewards and lower-score borrowers facing tighter access and higher costs. Replies add a counter-signal that rate caps may reduce access or shift costs into fees, showing how terms, pricing, rewards, and inclusion interact.
linked_research_question: How do card terms, credit-tier pricing, rewards, and dispute exposure distribute financial room and risk across consumers?
limits: The post is an interpretation of a CFPB report, not the underlying issuer-level panel
Replies are not representative borrower opinion
Policy claims about rate caps are prospective rather than observed outcomes
